 MOBILE, Ala. (NBC 15) — Federal prosecutors allege a Mobile tax preparation business helped submit more than 9,000 fraudulent tax returns that sought over $177 million in refunds. About $81 million was issued, according to an indictment.
 Kennedy Lawrence Stovall Winston, a former Blount High School and University of Alabama basketball player, is among six people charged in the case. The indictment, filed Sept. 23 in federal court in Mobile, accuses him and the others of conspiring to commit wire fraud.
 Winston is also charged in five counts of wire fraud. Prosecutors allege he and business owner Jennifer Beverly filed returns that claimed false federal fuel tax credits. The five returns, filed between January and February 2023, sought about $101,896 in refunds combined.
 The indictment says Beverly owned and operated JB Accounting Tax Service LLC in Mobile and supervised the other defendants, who worked as tax preparers. Prosecutors allege the group used false information to claim credits and deductions, including credits for fuel taxes and COVID-related sick or family leave, and reported businesses some clients did not own or operate.
 The indictment alleges the scheme ran from about 2022 through 2024. It lists 64 counts: one conspiracy count and 63 wire fraud counts involving specific tax returns. The defendants named in the filing face different counts.
 The government is also seeking forfeiture of alleged proceeds and several properties listed in the indictment.
 The charges are allegations. The defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.
